# `pi_station_set`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Configure the station-mode Wi-Fi connection and start an asynchronous connection check.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe4b10, ns_net::pi_station_set @0x6fd800, StartCheckStation @0x121ce0, CheckStaConnFunc @0x121710 (64-bit build); firmware 9.75 handler @0xfbec0 |

Writes the station network configuration for the given SSID and key via the network script, then starts (replacing any previous) a background check thread that watches for the connection until timeout_sec elapses. The reply reports only that setup and thread start succeeded; the outcome of the connection is obtained by polling pi_station_state or from the Station event, whose only producer is this check, which tests the connection about once a second until timeout_sec has passed, then sends Station complete or fail. On failure (timeout, an error from the check, or an address in 10.0.0.x) the device deletes the saved network it was trying to join before sending fail, so a client must re-send the credentials to retry. A newer pi_station_set stops the previous check without any event for it. If timeout_sec is not positive the error is returned after the configuration was already changed; nothing is rolled back on any error. Firmware 9.75 (64-bit build, app 3.4.0) the psk member (under params.para, no wifi object) is an enc1 token and needs the crypto session of the connection (secure-communication chapter); a missing session returns 570 and a bad token 571 to 573. Error 104 has an unresolved trigger in the 9.75 handler.

Side effects: Updates station network configuration (synchronous shell, no total timeout), stops the previous station-check thread, records the desired SSID and timeout and starts a new check thread. May cause the device to leave its current Wi-Fi network.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"pi_station_set"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | yes | - | Required. An object, or a one-element array whose first element is the object. In either case the object may itself carry a wrapper member para holding the real parameter object; when para is present it replaces the effective object, and a para that is not an object is rejected with 107. Unknown keys are ignored. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params absent or not an object, or para present and not an object | `expected object param` |
| 105 | ssid or psk not a string, or ssid missing/empty | `expected string param` |
| 104 | timeout_sec not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 106 | hidden not coercible to boolean | `expected bool param` |
| 570 | Firmware 9.75: no active crypto session, or the psk token cannot be decoded (571 invalid, 572 replay, 573 crypto failure) | `encrypted session required` |
| 209 | timeout_sec is 0 or negative (checked after configuration was written) | `invalid value` |
| 214 | The network script process could not be started | `fail to run command` |
| 207 | Script output contains the text error | `fail to operate` |
| 212 | The check thread could not be started (other thread-start codes may propagate) | `fail to create thread` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No result member on errors. The asynchronous connection outcome is reported by the Station event (or by polling pi_station_state), not by this reply.

## Example

Request, full - All members:

```json
{"id":91,"method":"pi_station_set","params":{"ssid":"ExampleNet","psk":"example-passphrase","timeout_sec":20,"hidden":false}}
```

Request, wrapped - Wrapper form with defaults:

```json
{"id":92,"method":"pi_station_set","params":{"para":{"ssid":"ExampleNet"}}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_set","result":0,"code":0,"id":91}
```

Reply, bad-timeout:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_set","error":"invalid value","code":209,"id":93}
```
